chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to me. He said: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi al-Qurashi narrated to me. He said: Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to me from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever fasts three days at the end of Sha'ban and connects them with the month of Ramadan, Allah shall record for him the fasting of two consecutive months.

key_terms.شَعْبَان: Sha'ban — the eighth month of the Islamic lunar calendar, considered a blessed month and a preparation for Ramadan
key_terms.صَوْم: sawm (fasting) — the voluntary abstention from food, drink, and other specified acts from dawn to sunset as an act of worship
key_terms.مُتَتَابِعَيْن: mutatabiʿayn (consecutive) — specifically two fasting periods that follow one another without interruption, giving double the spiritual reward

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for fasting the last three days of Sha'ban and connecting them with Ramadan?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that fasting the last three days of the month of Sha'ban and joining them with Ramadan earns the reward equivalent to fasting two complete consecutive months. This hadith was narrated in the Mashhad of Imam al-Ridha during the blessed month of Sha'ban in 368 AH, emphasizing the spiritual virtue of extending one's fast beyond Ramadan's formal beginning. The teaching reflects the Shia tradition of preparing spiritually for Ramadan through voluntary fasting in Sha'ban.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. `Ali Majiluwayh (rh) narrated to us. He said: My uncle Muhammad b. Abi’l Qasim narrated to me. He said: Muhammad b. `Ali al-Kufi al-Qurashi narrated to me. He said: Muhammad b. Sinan narrated to me from al-Mufaddal b. `Umar from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad (as). He said:
Whoever fasts three days at the end of Sha`ban and connects it with the month of Ramadan, Allah shall record the fasting of two consecutive months for him.
